Budesonide vs Standard Care for Early COVID-19: For clinical recovery time, the mean difference was -4.00 days (95% CI: -6.16 to -1.84), indicating that patients treated with budesonide recovered approximately 4 days faster than those receiving standard care. Regarding urgent hospital visits, the risk ratio was 0.18 (95% CI: 0.04 to 0.79), suggesting that patients on budesonide were significantly less likely to require urgent hospital visits compared to those on standard care. 2. Budesonide vs Standard Care for High-Risk Patients: For mortality, the risk ratio was 0.61 (95% CI: 0.22 to 1.67), indicating no statistically significant reduction in death risk with budesonide compared to standard care. Clinical recovery time showed a mean difference of -1.00 days (95% CI: -1.58 to -0.42), meaning that high-risk patients treated with budesonide recovered about 1 day faster than those receiving standard care. For alleviation of all symptoms, the risk ratio was 0.99 (95% CI: 0.96 to 1.02), showing no significant difference between the two groups. The risk ratio for intensive care unit (ICU) admission was 0.48 (95% CI: 0.23 to 1.01), suggesting a potential but not statistically significant reduction in ICU admissions with budesonide. For mechanical ventilation, the risk ratio was 0.94 (95% CI: 0.44 to 1.98), indicating no significant difference in the need for mechanical ventilation between the two groups. 3. Ciclesonide vs Standard Care for Mild to Moderate COVID-19: Mortality at 28–30 days had a risk ratio of 0.19 (95% CI: 0.01 to 3.96), showing no statistically significant difference in death rates between ciclesonide and standard care. Clinical improvement at 14 days had a risk ratio of 1.10 (95% CI: 0.96 to 1.27), indicating no significant difference in improvement rates between the two groups. Hospitalization at 14 days had a risk ratio of 1.01 (95% CI: 0.45 to 2.25), showing no significant difference in hospitalization rates. The duration of hospitalization had a mean difference of -0.40 days (95% CI: -4.22 to 3.42), indicating no significant reduction in hospital stay duration with ciclesonide. Clinical improvement at 7 days had a risk ratio of 1.08 (95% CI: 0.83 to 1.40), showing no significant difference in improvement rates at 7 days between ciclesonide and standard care.
